content:
marta: quick postmortem from the canary of the "dual-window" limiter. saw several high-burst tenants get hard-ejected immediately instead of being slowed. i want to capture design followups and an ops playbook here. :clipboard:

alex: thanks for filing. root cause seems to be the current rule evaluating a blended score (short * weight_short + long * weight_long) and comparing to one threshold. spikes dominated blended score and triggered hard eject.

sam: tl;dr: blending is too aggressive. suggestion: decouple into two-tier logic: short_window -> short_action, long_window -> fairness_action. only escalate to hard eject when both short_window_abuse AND sustained_long_term_violation are true. otherwise apply token-bucket throttling + probation.

cheng: concrete: short_window window=20s, metric=peak_rps_ratio; long_window=1h, metric=quantile(0.95)_request_share. policy: if short_peak > 0.9 -> mark short_hit; if long_share > 0.7 -> mark long_hit. hard_eject if short_hit AND long_hit. else if short_hit only -> soft_probation (drop priority, reduce concurrency by 40% for 5m).

tariq: add host-side SLO telemetry: 99th latency and queue_depth. If tail latency spikes correlate 1:1 with tenant short_hits, escalate faster. this avoids noisy tests that don't impact host health.

julie: sample config (for RFC appendix):
```json
{
  "short_window_s": "20",
  "short_metric": "peak_rps_ratio",
  "short_threshold": "0.90",
  "short_action": "soft_probation",
  "soft_probation_seconds": "300",
  "probation_reduction_pct": "40",
  "long_window_s": "3600",
  "long_metric": "p95_request_share",
  "long_threshold": "0.70",
  "hard_eject_condition": "short_hit && long_hit",
  "hard_eject_ttl_s": "1800",
  "use_tail_latency": "true",
  "tail_latency_threshold_ms": "1200",
  "reserved_tier_behavior": "skip_soft; alert+pager",
  "decay_alpha": "0.12"
}
```

marta: ops note: reserved/dedicated customers (customer_tier==reserved) must skip soft probation and instead enter the SLA path: immediate alert to eng-sre, throttle at ingress but do not evict. we should surface a fast path so oncall knows to escalate to account team.

nora: agree. also surface the tenant owner/email in the alert. we had one case where we lacked owner metadata and wasted time tracing.

alex: telemetry + alerting checklist to implement before wider rollout:
- per-tenant: short_hits (counter)
- per-tenant: probation_entries (counter)
- per-tenant: hard_ejections_total (counter)
- per-host: tail_latency_violations (counter)
- alert: hard_eject_rate > 0.5%/min (prod)
- alert: probation_rate > 2%/5m (prod)
- dashboard: ejection waterfall (short->probation->hard) with tenant drilldown

sam: add synthetic test cases: rapid burst (5k rps for 10s), noisy-onboard (frequent small bursts), clinic tests where many tenants burst together. need to ensure soft_probation recovers correctly.

cheng: escalation logic discussion: should probation be probabilistic (p-drop) or deterministic (reduce concurrency)? probabilistic dropping smooths client spikes better, deterministic reduction is easier to reason about. tradeoff: p-drop can interact badly with fairness because it's statistical.

marta: go with deterministic concurrency cap for now (easier for SLO reasoning). we can iterate later with a/b tests.

tariq: operational playbook sketch (eng-sre):
- alert fires: hard_eject_rate > threshold -> oncall page
- oncall: run `tenant-inspect --id=<tenant> --since=now-10m` (shows short_hits, p95 latency, owner)
- if reserved tier: immediately notify account team and follow SLA checklist
- otherwise: if host tail latency high, confirm eject; if not, revert eject and apply longer probation window
- document rollback command: `rlsctl eject --tenant <id> --undo`

julie: add logs example for tracing: `2025-09-12T14:24:57Z host-19 short_hit tenant=acme-42 peak_rps=512 short_thresh=450 action=soft_probation rev=0.9`

marta: who owns final RFC update + config rollout? eng-platform to own RFC + template config. eng-sre to own runbook + pager mapping. i'll draft the RFC update and ping @eng-sre for acceptance.

nora: can we add a feature flag per region so we can roll changes gradually? also need a safe default that disables hard_eject unless enabled by flag.

alex: yes. feature flag: `enable_hard_eject` default=false. rollout plan: canary region -> two more regions -> global. monitor probation rate and hard ejects per region after each step.

sam: timeline suggestion: RFC update this week, implement telemetry & flags next sprint, limited canary after tests, full rollout in 3 sprints if stable.

marta: thanks all. i'll drop a PR with the RFC diff + config appendix and link to synthetic test harness. tagging followups: @eng-sre for runbook, @eng-ml for anomaly-detection tuning later. :eyes:
